## **5.3.2 Exacerbation trials: HZC102871 and HZC102970**

To demonstrate efficacy, GSK submitted the results of four pivotal phase 3 clinical trials: two replicate 24-week lung function trials (2206 and 2207) and two 52-week exacerbation trials (2871 and 2970).

design.text: 52-week, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, multicenter trial randomizing 1:1:1:1 to FF/VI 50/25, 100/25, 200/25 mcg or VI 25 mcg once daily

citations.quote: This trial was a randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, multi-center trial evaluating 3, once-daily dosage strengths of FF/VI compared to VI 25 mcg.
Patients who met randomization criteria were then randomized 1:1:1:1 to one of four treatment groups: FF/VI 50/25 mcg, FF/VI 100/25 mcg, FF/VI 200/25 mcg or VI 25 mcg.

population.text: COPD patients with a documented history of at least one COPD exacerbation within 12 months of screening

citations.quote: Trial 871 enrolled a similar patient population as trial 2206. However instead of baseline dyspnea symptoms requirement, subjects had to have a documented history of \ge 1 COPD exacerbation within 12 months of screening.

endpoint.text: Annual rate of moderate and severe exacerbations

citations.quote: Both exacerbation trials evaluated the annual rate of moderate and severe exacerbations as the primary endpoint with the primary comparison of interest between each dose of FF/VI and VI.

indication.text: Combination ICS/LABA indicated for long-term, once-daily maintenance treatment of airflow obstruction in COPD, including chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema, and to reduce exacerbations of COPD in patients with a history of exacerbations; NOT indicated for acute bronchospasm or asthma

citations.quote: BREO ELLIPTA is a combination inhaled corticosteroid/long-acting beta2-adrenergic agonist (ICS/LABA) indicated for the long-term, once-daily, maintenance treatment of airflow obstruction in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), including chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema. BREO ELLIPTA is also indicated to reduce exacerbations of COPD in patients with a history of exacerbations.
**Important Limitations of Use:** BREO ELLIPTA is NOT indicated for the relief of acute bronchospasm or for the treatment of asthma.

target_moa.text: Fixed combination of fluticasone furoate, a synthetic corticosteroid with anti-inflammatory activity, and vilanterol, a long-acting beta2-adrenergic agonist (LABA) bronchodilator — two different classes of medication

citations.quote: These drugs represent 2 different classes of medications (a synthetic corticosteroid and a LABA) that have different effects on clinical and physiological indices.
**Fluticasone Furoate:** Fluticasone furoate is a synthetic trifluorinated corticosteroid with anti-inflammatory activity.
**Vilanterol:** Vilanterol is a LABA.

modality.text: Small molecule (inhaled corticosteroid + long-acting beta2-agonist dry powder inhalation)

citations.quote: Breo Ellipta is a new combination inhalation product comprised of an inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) and a long-acting beta-agonist (LABA).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=3%): nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection, headache, and oral candidiasis. In 6-month trials, nasopharyngitis 9% (FF/VI 100/25) vs 8% placebo and headache 7% vs 5% placebo. Increased incidence of pneumonia: in 12-month trials in 3,255 subjects, FF/VI 100/25 pneumonia 6% (51 of 806) vs vilanterol 3% (27 of 818)

In replicate 12-month trials in 3,255 subjects with COPD who had experienced a COPD exacerbation in the previous year, there was a higher incidence of pneumonia reported in subjects receiving the fluticasone furoate/vilanterol combination (50 mcg/25 mcg: 6% [48 of 820 subjects]; 100 mcg/25 mcg: 6% [51 of 806 subjects]; or 200 mcg/25 mcg: 7% [55 of 811 subjects]) than in subjects receiving vilanterol 25 mcg (3% [27 of 818 subjects]).

detail.text: WARNING: ASTHMA-RELATED DEATH — LABA, such as vilanterol, increase the risk of asthma-related death; a placebo-controlled US trial with another LABA (salmeterol) showed an increase in asthma-related deaths, considered a class effect of all LABA

citations.quote: ## WARNING: ASTHMA-RELATED DEATH

Long-acting beta2-adrenergic agonists (LABA) increase the risk of asthma-related death. Data from a large placebo-controlled US trial that compared the safety of another LABA (salmeterol) with placebo added to usual asthma therapy showed an increase in asthma-related deaths in subjects receiving salmeterol.
